sequencing_rationale: This wave is almost entirely Elm and three files are contended: Main.elm (6a, 6b), Api.elm (6c, 6d), Bookshelf.elm (6f, 6d). The DAG is shaped by file ownership rather than pure logic — two agents in one Elm module is a merge conflict by construction (the #343/#344 lesson). 6a goes first because AuthState is the type every later auth change reads.
notes: Founding defect, root-caused live 2026-07-30: the auth credential is downstream of a browser animation frame. With the window occluded, WAAPI never fires, so three login 200s were silently discarded — ten frozen 300ms transitions, zero animations, no follow-up XHR.
The epic's own warning: do NOT write per-page 401 tests before the wrapper lands (6c) — they would be deleted by it.
#332 was assigned to this wave by owner ruling during Wave 3; it is a production mutation guard living in the view instead of the update function.

coordination_decisions.issue: The 3-tuple OutMsg session-expiry convention (~25 sites) requires Main.elm routing blocks, but Main.elm was assigned to #360 at this level. A page cannot reach the expiry net alone — requestStoredAuth/clearAuth/Nav.pushUrl all live in Main.
coordination_decisions.decision: #361 makes the three additive Main.elm blocks, mirroring Consent.SessionExpired exactly, staged last and isolated. It also takes the redirectAfterLogin-on-expiry fix (#359 finding) since forceSessionExpiry is session-expiry logic and #360 has no reason to touch it.
coordination_decisions.merge_order_changed: 361 now merges BEFORE 360; #360 re-merges the integration branch and reconciles in its own worktree rather than the lead hand-resolving Elm conflicts at the merge point.
coordination_decisions.why: The type system forces it: pages returning 3-tuples do not compile against a Main.elm expecting 2-tuples, so no Main-free variant of #361 could build or test itself. The alternative (page-local expiry banner) would invent a 26th convention and bypass the cross-tab re-check net.
